sentences: QMA uses a single quantum witness, while \(\mathrm{QMA}(2)\) permits two witnesses that must be unentangled across a specified division.
This question asks how much verification power that unentanglement promise adds.
The cited work studies proofs with restricted relative phases and finds that nearby models can have very different complexity.
Those results do not directly establish equality or separation for ordinary QMA and \(\mathrm{QMA}(2)\).
Understanding the relationship would isolate whether independently supplied quantum proofs provide an advantage unavailable to one unrestricted quantum certificate.
